<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via PageSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object pageKindJsxToHtml), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object pageKindJsxToHtml))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19a19bd1898e24742059dea73e169fa3fabb9cf0` — the merge of head `2e1b65d066242d602f855ba62d5e4f247a09871b` into base `23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19a19bd1898e24742059dea73e169fa3fabb9cf0 && git checkout 19a19bd1898e24742059dea73e169fa3fabb9cf0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c 2e1b65d066242d602f855ba62d5e4f247a09871b && git checkout -B drift-repro 23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c && git merge --no-ff 2e1b65d066242d602f855ba62d5e4f247a09871b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 23e689dc7d1de961a168997685295ddf009d5c2c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T08:15Z

This is the seat review of record for #23543 family F5-jsx (claim `6185261661`, ruling `6182001882` items 5 and 7) on head:

`831a9fa8ea`

It is not the contract review. That review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`Clause-②: yes`, narrowing: a retired published spec value).

1. **Form.**
   - Draft to `main`. The first line is `Part of #23543`, the body has no closing keyword, and `Clause-②: yes` sits at the start of a line.
   - 43 files, +394/−198. Not governed: `check-governed-merges --pr 23638` reads NOT governed.
   - A BREAKING changeset grades `spec` `minor`, beside `patch` for the runtime readers.
   - The one generated path is `content/docs/references/ui/page.mdx` (`merge=os-regen`). It was regenerated after `main` was merged through `os-regen-merge.sh`, and `main` has not touched it since the merge base.
2. **Against the ruling.**
   - `'jsx'` retires from `PageSchema.kind` through `enumWithRetiredValues`, with the prescription naming `html`. `tsc` and the parse refuse it.
   - `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` is `['html']`. `page-kind-jsx-to-html` sets `retiredFromLoadPath`, and a D3 entry records the retirement.
   - Every non-test `'jsx'` reader in `metadata-protocol`, `cli` and `lint` drops its branch, with no consumer-side tolerance left.
   - `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` and every other entry are untouched.
3. **Mechanism assumptions measured.**
   - Stored rows: the rehydration seams replay the retired entry, so a stored `jsx` page loads as `html`, which is pinned. The save door refuses `jsx` with a `422`.
   - The `os migrate meta` suites that had `jsx` as their live subject are re-pointed, as F1's review foresaw.
   - The three translated help strings are hand edits that their files' own header sanctions ("Edit translations in place"). The key sets are unchanged, and `check:i18n` passes.
4. **Gates.**
   - Locally: 118 derived families, 116 run, 2 NOT MEASURED (shallow clone; full build). `check:platform-checklist` is red on `main`'s tree, outside this diff.
   - An ablation of the prescription went red as predicted and was restored.
   - CI on `831a9fa8ea` is converging, and landing waits on every check.
5. **Accepted deviations.** The files beyond the claim's surface are each a pin-sweep or false-text hit, named in the report: the docs pages, the D3 rationale texts, the re-pointed suites and the translated strings. This record amends the claim's surface to the PR's file list.
6. **The dev's open question: A, deferred to the same file's Tier H PR.**
   - `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md:138` still calls `jsx` an alias of `html`, and that file is governed.
   - #23610's execution already owes a Tier H PR on the same file (the `home` / `utility` rows and the template region names). This sentence rides that PR, and the seat's ledger carries it until then. This PR stays contract-tier.
7. **Out-of-scope findings.**
   - **objectui:** the value is read in more places than the one console sample (the `PageNodeSchema.kind` union in `packages/types/src/layout.ts`, a `kind === 'jsx'` branch in the page renderer, the types zod mirror). The seat posts them on objectstack-ai/objectui#12334, the ruling's objectui half, at landing.
   - The F5-http dependency of the re-pointed suites, and the `check:platform-checklist` red, are noted.
8. **Landing terms.** First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green. Then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge. On merge, #23543 is released to `pm:queue` with F3, F2, F4 and F5-http left.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `831a9fa8eaa189ba7c0c57f84f8e0cf5f3ed2c4d`
Local-runs: none

Family F5-jsx of ruling 6182001882 (items 5 and 7) on card #23543, PR #23638, read at 2026-10-15T08:32Z. Inputs: the card body and its thirteen comments, the PR body and its 43-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge-base `f7cd580bff` (+394/−198, equal to the three-dot diff against `origin/main`), and the check-runs on this head, read twice. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every tree reading below is `git show` / `git grep` against the fetched head, and the objectui readings are against the pinned `.objectui-sha` `b9814b334`.

**Gate verdicts on this head** (second reading): 44 check-runs, 33 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 3 `in_progress`. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (and its four lanes), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` (both firings), `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the nine `Lint ·` lanes, and the card, claim, single-writer and Part-of guards are all `success`; `Test Core` 2/6, 5/6 and 6/6 are `success`. **NOT MEASURED at this reading:** `Test Core` 1/6, 3/6 and 4/6 (`in_progress`) and therefore the `Test Core` aggregate; landing waits on them whatever this record says. The 8 `skipped` are the PR fast-set skips (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`, both opt-in packed-tarball smokes, the re-fired `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` duplicates), measured by `main`'s full battery, not on the PR.

Governance: none of the 43 paths is a governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` `success`; by eye no `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`); head repo equals base repo; `Part of #23543` is the first line and no closing keyword follows; draft; no `content/docs/releases/` edit (the drift check's read-only row was left alone, correctly).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes (each narrows what an author may write):

1. **`PageSchema.kind` refuses `jsx` by name** (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts`): `enumWithRetiredValues(['full', 'slotted', 'html', 'react'], PAGE_KIND_RETIRED_GUIDANCE).default('full')`. The helper returns a plain `z.enum` with an error map (`shared/retired-key.ts`), so `z.input` drops the member (`tsc` refuses it), `.default`, `.options` and the JSON Schema projection follow the four-member enum, and the helper's own constructor guards (a retired name may not stay in `values`, the prescription may not be blank) hold by construction. An authored `jsx` is refused at `kind` with the prescription ("Page `kind: 'jsx'` was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0087 D2) … Use `kind: 'html'`"); a misspelling (`htm`) keeps zod's own message (pinned as the control); at `defineStack` it is `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 with the ONE issue at `pages.0.kind` (the fixture is otherwise a complete html page, so nothing else can fire). **RIGHT** — ruling F5-jsx A's "retire `'jsx'` from `PageSchema.kind` through `enumWithRetiredValues` naming `html`", and item 7's "`tsc` and the parse-time prescription are the whole channel". The prescription carries no `os migrate meta` sentence, rightly: the conversion is protocol 11 and `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` is 16 (`migrations/registry.ts.template:79`), so the tool lists nothing for it. The published JSON Schema `ui/Page` narrows with it; `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` is a names-only list, so no regeneration is owed and none is missing.
2. **`COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` is `['html']`**, `checkPageSourceCompleteness` reads `html` / `react`, and the `checkPageRequiresKind` refusal no longer sends an author to `jsx` (pinned: the message contains `html` and not `jsx`). **RIGHT** — the ruling's "together with the `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` branch". The exported tuple's type narrows from two members to one; `api-surface/ui.json` records `"COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS (const)"` by name only, so `check:api-surface` cannot see this narrowing — the changeset is its carrier, judged in ②.
3. **`page-kind-jsx-to-html` leaves the load path** (`conversions/registry.ts`, the only hunk in that file: the docblock and the two new fields; `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` and every other entry untouched): `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` — the value the seven #23487 retirements and F1 carry, pinned by `retired-after.census`. The authoring funnel no longer rewrites an authored `jsx` (pinned: the stack comes back equal, zero notices), so the author meets judgment 1. **The stored-row path holds, and through one seam:** `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (`conversions/stored.ts`) hard-codes `includeRetired: true`; `metadata-protocol` reaches it only through `convertStoredItemDetailed` (`protocol.ts:6444`), which every stored-row reader funnels into via `convertStoredItem` — eleven call sites on the head: boot hydration, get, list, draft, overlay, package duplication and `migrateStoredMetadata` among them — and `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts:874` is the second reader. The artifact door replays a retired entry while the artifact's declared floor is at or below its `retiredAfter` (`artifact-forward-conversion.ts:37`), which is what the changeset says. So a `sys_metadata` page row written as `jsx` reaches `PageSchema` as `html`; pinned in `conversions.test.ts` (`applyConversionsToStoredItem('page', …)` → `html`, and the converted row parses). **RIGHT.**
4. **The save door refuses, it does not convert.** `resolveOverlaySchema` → `getMetadataTypeSchema('page')` → `safeParse(request.item)` (`protocol.ts:820`, `:22562`); only `flow` gets a verdict-time `applyConversionsToFlow`. A page saved with `kind: 'jsx'` is therefore 422 `INVALID_METADATA` with the prescription at `kind`, as the changeset and the D3 entry state. **RIGHT** — and it is the substance of item 7's "no double spelling": after this PR no door accepts the spelling from an author or an API caller; only data at rest is converged, and only on the seam that replays retired entries.
5. **Every reader of the retired value dropped its branch; none tolerates it.** Head-tree sweep of `packages/*/src` outside tests for the quoted value: zero hits. `metadata-protocol` `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` (its one read, `:739`, the html-page compile gate — a stored `jsx` row reaches it as `html` by judgment 3); `cli/src/utils/sdui-manifest.ts` `checkedPageKeys` (`html` only); `lint` `page-walk.ts` `SOURCE_AUTHORED_KINDS`, `validate-jsx-pages.ts` and `validate-page-source-styling.ts` (`html` / `react`); the rest comments. The three lint rules now yield nothing for a `jsx` page (pinned as "does NOT read"): that is non-reading, not acceptance — `os lint` does not Zod-parse by design (`lint.ts:623`), and the refusal is the parse's at `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build` and the save door. **RIGHT.** One wording point on that list is in ③.
6. **Verdict-list pin** (`conversions.test.ts`): the kept-without-ruling list drops to the six entries of F3, F2, F4 and F5-http; the retired list gains the entry with `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`; the new `describe('page-kind-jsx-to-html')` pins the three claims that must hold together (stored row converges and parses; funnel no longer rewrites; `defineStack` refuses naming `html` and the release, with `html` and `htm` as controls); `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` gains the refusal row in its `JOIN`, so every retired entry still has a renderer. The `excludeConversionIds` firing control still drives this entry under `includeRetired: true`, so it still fires; its comment is corrected. **RIGHT** — item 7's "verdict-list pin updated".
7. **D3 entry `18.page-kind-jsx-retired.ts`** — a `SemanticMigration` in the sibling shape, with no `conversionIds`. **RIGHT:** `page-kind-jsx-to-html` is in no step's `conversionIds` on the head (protocol 11 is below the floor), and `migrations.test.ts:80` refuses a link no step replays; ADR-0087 D2's "graduates into the D3 chain" cannot apply to a conversion older than the chain, and the entry says so. The `check:adr-0087-registration` marker names this id; `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` rode green inside `Lint & Repo Gates`.
8. **Re-pointed suites.** The three cli e2e suites (nightly tier — not run by the PR's `Test Core`; the dev's local 3 files / 35 passed is the only reading), `stack-conversions-record.test.ts` and two `conversions.test.ts` cases now drive `flow-node-http-callout-rename` (live, protocol 11); metadata-core `artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts` FIRING CONTROL 1 drives `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen` (live, F4's entry). **RIGHT for F5-jsx**; the cost is carried in ③ with one precision the report lacks.
9. **Fixture triage**: the `html` re-spellings keep their assertions; the deleted `jsx` rows pinned the deleted branch; `protocol.batch-verb-driver-text.test.ts` P13 still seeds a stored `jsx` row, which is still a non-canonical row the stored pass rewrites (judgment 3), so a comment was the right edit; `format.conversion-notice.test.ts` formats a synthetic notice. **RIGHT.**
10. **Text edits beyond the claim's surface state only what is true**, each checked against the head: `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` and `react-pages.mdx` (retired at 18, refused with the prescription, stored pages keep loading — true by judgments 1 and 3); the generated `references/ui/page.mdx` matches the new `.describe()` text; `page.form.ts`'s `visibleWhen` and help text; the four translation bundles, where the three hand edits drop exactly the alias parenthetical and the key set is unchanged (`check:i18n` OK, `Spec property liveness` and `Lint & Repo Gates` `success`); the two D3 entries, the step-18 rationale and `liveness/page.json`'s `requires` evidence. **RIGHT.** Residues the sweep found: `liveness/page.json`'s `requires` row keeps a sentence in its `note` that now over-states ("the key exists only on kind 'html' / 'jsx' pages") — the same row whose `evidence` the diff corrected; `page.form.ts:51`'s comment still says "the three source-compiled kinds" (there are two); `docs/adr/0081` still says `'jsx'` stays a deprecated alias (Tier H, superseded in fact by the ruling); `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md:138` (the dev's open question). The `source` row's note names objectui's `kind:'jsx'` renderer branch, which is still true at the pin. All four are in ③.

Public-surface changes: no new export (`PAGE_KIND_RETIRED_GUIDANCE` is module-private; `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` are unchanged, as the dev reports). The one widening is the published migration catalogue gaining the D3 entry (judgment 7), the same half F1's record counted.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23543-f5-jsx-retire-page-kind-jsx.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`; `metadata-protocol`, `cli`, `lint`: `patch`; `feat(spec)!:`; `**BREAKING (authoring):**` banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; FROM → TO (`kind: 'jsx'` → `kind: 'html'`, and the API caller's one-word change); the honest statement that `os migrate meta` does not list the edit; how stored rows and artifacts keep loading; the ADR-0087 disposition marker `registered page-kind-jsx-retired`, whose id exists (judgment 7). The repo is in Changesets pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), where a BREAKING spec change grades `minor`; the frontmatter, banner and arm match F1's changeset on the head byte-for-shape. `Check Changeset` is `success` on both firings; `check-adr-0087-registration` rode green. The three runtime readers' `patch` is **RIGHT**: `metadata-protocol`'s and `cli`'s changed constants are module-private, `lint`'s exported rules change behaviour only on an input the spec no longer admits, and none of the three narrows a surface of its own — the narrowing is the spec row's, and the body names what each reader now reads.
- **WRONG: `@objectstack/platform-objects` publishes and has no row.** The diff changes `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/{en,zh-CN,ja-JP,es-ES}.metadata-forms.generated.ts` — the Studio page form's `source` help text in four locales — and `@objectstack/platform-objects` is a published package (`18.0.0-next.1`, not private). The precedent is explicit and uniform: the last six landings that touched this bundle each carry `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch` with a one-line body row, three of them retirements of exactly this shape (#23488 `23488-admin-scope-binding-authoring-retired.md`, #22876 `22876-email-template-category-is-system-retired.md`, #23395 `23395-page-form-empty-state.md`). AGENTS.md Post-Task #3 ("Add a changeset for anything that publishes … a `patch` changeset — never none") is the rule. `Check Changeset` stayed green because its two scripts (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs`) read the bump level and the Clause-② line, not per-package coverage; this record is where coverage is judged. The changeset does not match what the diff publishes, so the verdict below is FAIL; the remedy is one frontmatter row and one body line.
- **The `Clause-②:` line.** The changeset's `yes (narrowing)` is the ruling's arm and the right one (a D3 entry widens the catalogue; judgments 1–4 narrow). The PR body's line reads bare `Clause-②: yes`, which `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines as "a widening" with no arm — the same gap F1's record flagged (③ item 1 there), with the same provenance: the claim comment 6185261661 wrote the bare line and the dev copied it as instructed. F1 landed with its body line unamended, so no gate turns on it (`check-changeset-no-major` reads `yes` and finds `spec` at `minor`; the breaking-signal reader takes the arm from the changeset). Not a verdict condition; ③ item 3.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (6187521557):

1. *`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md:138` still calls `jsx` a deprecated alias; the file is Tier H.* **Answered: A**, as the seat review 6187645640 already routed it: the sentence rides #23610's Tier H PR on the same file, the seat's ledger carries it until then, and this PR stays contract-tier. Confirmed present on the head. Escalated beside it, same carrier, the seat's choice: `docs/adr/0081` (status line and decisions 1 and 6) still records `'jsx'` as a kept deprecated alias; ruling 6182001882 is the decision of record that retires it, and a dated status note on ADR-0081 citing the ruling would keep Prime Directive #13's "an ADR binds until a superseding record says otherwise" findable. Not a condition of this record.

Dev `deviations`:

2. *Files beyond the claim's surface.* **Accepted** — each is a pin-sweep or false-text hit named in the report and re-checked in ① judgments 8–10; the seat review amended the claim's surface to the file list.
3. *`metadata-protocol`, `cli`, `lint` at `patch`.* **Accepted** (②). *The body's `Clause-②` line.* The seat spells the arm at source in the F3 claim's line, and amends this body to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` if it touches the body for the FAIL remedy anyway — one line, read back, no second footer.
4. *Worktree cut from a newer `main`; the model-named trailer not used.* **Accepted** — process notes; `check:commit-card-trailers` rode green on every push and the merge from `origin/main` `f7cd580b` came through `os-regen-merge.sh` with `check:generated` reading all 14 up to date.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`:

5. *objectui reads the retired value in more places than the ruling's one console sample.* **Verified at the pin `b9814b334`:** `packages/types/src/layout.ts:1795` (`kind?: 'full' | 'slotted' | 'html' | 'jsx' | 'react'` on the interface that extends the spec's `Page`), `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx:611` (`kind === 'html' || kind === 'jsx'`), `apps/console/src/sdui-jsx-preview.tsx:87` (`kind: 'jsx'`).
